steps.speaker: Cyrus
steps.content: Who's here to challenge the marvelous Cyrus?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Player Cyrus has already been kicked out... You're just a regular NPC now.

steps.speaker: Cyrus
steps.content: Watch your tongue! Chosen One, do you intend to challenge the marvelous Cyrus?
Cyrus ignores your metagaming remark and goes on spouting the same nonsense in the script. Still the same maniacal, arrogant, lofty clichés of a stereotypical final boss.
Why must they make the final boss the villain?
The hero wants to save the world with his power. The final boss wants to rule the world with his power. The two ideas are not fundamentally contradictory.
The more stereotypical the plot, the easier it is to deconstruct and twist it. It just so happens that you're excellent at spotting the loopholes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Challenge? Of course not. I'm here to help you, Cyrus.
You take out a white dice from the pocket and gently place it on your palm.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is the Chosen One's token. It carries a great deal of the Dragon of Genesis' power. Outside the curtain of the world, the Game Master decides all our actions with this dice.
Cyrus stares at you in confusion, his previous pretentiousness suddenly all gone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: A final boss unchallenged by the hero is worthless. Even though it's your goal to become the Dragon of Genesis, you can't just waste your time in this castle until doomsday.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But don't worry, open your mind a little. Who says there is only one dice representing fate and only one the Chosen One?
You gently turn the dice in your hand, but somehow feel obstructed by some invisible force.
Cyrus stares at the white dice and produces the power source from his chest hesitantly.
The shell unfolds to reveal a similar twenty-sided dark-purple dice inside.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who says a boss must be a villain? As long as one has the power to change the world, one can become the protagonist of the story.

steps.speaker: Cyrus
steps.content: The protagonist?
The invisible strings binding the dice loosen. You apply more strength with your hand.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The protagonist is the winner who beats all the challenges. We both have a piece of the Dragon of Genesis' power fragments. Why fight when we can team up? I'll give you the white one, but you'll come with me. Let's resurrect the Dragon of Genesis.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: After all, we have the same final goal in this game. To clear it.

steps.speaker: Cyrus
steps.content: ...To clear it? ...To clear it. Right, I must clear the game!
Suddenly, you hear a tearing sound from the void. The strings have been broken.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's challenge fate! Cyrus, welcome to the player's team.
The dice spin. With a white flash, the dark-purple and white dice fall to the ground quietly.
<color=#fb9259>Critical Success</color>. It looks like even the Game Master can't dispute this.

steps.speaker: Game Master
steps.content: <color=#7683a2><size=44>You! You're cheating!</color></size>

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Does the rulebook forbid the hero from teaming up with the final boss? It's an unconventional approach, indeed. But with only 24 hours left, we're in hell mode, gotta take a few shortcuts, okay?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Let's go. Time to rewrite the script.
